claim: A key limiting factor of successful axon regeneration is the intrinsic regenerative ability in both the peripheral nervous system (PNS) and central nervous system (CNS).
source: A key limiting factor of successful axon regeneration is the intrinsic regenerative ability in both the peripheral nervous system (PNS) and central nervous system (CNS).
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established scientific understanding about axon regeneration.

claim: Previous studies have identified intrinsic regenerative ability regulators that act on gene expression in injured neurons.
source: Previous studies have identified intrinsic regenerative ability regulators that act on gene expression in injured neurons.
evidence: This statement references prior research findings.

claim: It is less known whether RNA modifications play a role in axon regeneration.
source: However, it is less known whether RNA modifications play a role in this process.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge.

claim: ALKBH5 is an evolutionarily conserved RNA m6A demethylase.
source: Here, we systematically screened the functions of all common m6A modification-related enzymes in axon regeneration and report ALKBH5, an evolutionarily conserved RNA m6A demethylase, as a regulator of axonal regeneration in rodents.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the nature of ALKBH5.

claim: ALKBH5 is a regulator of axonal regeneration in rodents.
source: Here, we systematically screened the functions of all common m6A modification-related enzymes in axon regeneration and report ALKBH5, an evolutionarily conserved RNA m6A demethylase, as a regulator of axonal regeneration in rodents.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on systematic screening.

claim: Knockdown of ALKBH5 enhanced sensory axonal regeneration in PNS.
source: In PNS, knockdown of ALKBH5 enhanced sensory axonal regeneration, whereas overexpressing ALKBH5 impaired axonal regeneration in an m6A-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the study.

claim: Overexpressing ALKBH5 impaired axonal regeneration in an m6A-dependent manner.
source: In PNS, knockdown of ALKBH5 enhanced sensory axonal regeneration, whereas overexpressing ALKBH5 impaired axonal regeneration in an m6A-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the study.

claim: ALKBH5 increased the stability of Lpin2 mRNA.
source: Mechanistically, ALKBH5 increased the stability of Lpin2 mRNA and thus limited regenerative growth associated lipid metabolism in dorsal root ganglion neurons.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study.

claim: ALKBH5 limited regenerative growth associated lipid metabolism in dorsal root ganglion neurons.
source: Mechanistically, ALKBH5 increased the stability of Lpin2 mRNA and thus limited regenerative growth associated lipid metabolism in dorsal root ganglion neurons.
evidence: This is a mechanistic finding from the study.

claim: Knockdown of ALKBH5 enhanced the survival and axonal regeneration of retinal ganglion cells after optic nerve injury in CNS.
source: Moreover, in CNS, knockdown of ALKBH5 enhanced the survival and axonal regeneration of retinal ganglion cells after optic nerve injury.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the study.

claim: Triggering axon regeneration, accelerating nerve regeneration, and extending the regenerated nerve length are the most straightforward methods of nerve repair following injury.
source: Triggering axon regeneration, accelerating nerve regeneration, and extending the regenerated nerve length are the most straightforward methods of nerve repair following injury (Costigan et al., 2002; Moore and Goldberg, 2011; Palmisano et al., 2019; Smith and Skene, 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Axon regeneration processes are highly dependent on the intrinsic regeneration ability of neurons.
source: These processes are highly dependent on the intrinsic regeneration ability of neurons.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: Diminished intrinsic regeneration ability is one of the major barriers for axonal regeneration following nerve injury.
source: However, diminished intrinsic regeneration ability is one of the major barriers for axonal regeneration following nerve injury.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: CNS and PNS possess distinct regenerative outcomes.
source: Although central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS) possess distinct regenerative outcomes, recent studies suggested that these neurons share certain molecular mechanisms that regulate their regenerative capacity.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: CNS and PNS neurons share certain molecular mechanisms that regulate their regenerative capacity.
source: Although central nervous system (CNS) and peripheral nervous system (PNS) possess distinct regenerative outcomes, recent studies suggested that these neurons share certain molecular mechanisms that regulate their regenerative capacity.
evidence: This statement is supported by recent studies.

claim: Pten has been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
source: For example, genes such as Pten (Liu et al., 2010; Park et al., 2008), Lin28 (Nathan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018a), Socs3/Jak (Smith et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2011), Atf3 (Seijffers et al., 2006; Seijffers et al., 2007), and Cbp/P300 (Hutson et al., 2019; Müller et al., 2022) have been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Lin28 has been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
source: For example, genes such as Pten (Liu et al., 2010; Park et al., 2008), Lin28 (Nathan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018a), Socs3/Jak (Smith et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2011), Atf3 (Seijffers et al., 2006; Seijffers et al., 2007), and Cbp/P300 (Hutson et al., 2019; Müller et al., 2022) have been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Socs3/Jak has been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
source: For example, genes such as Pten (Liu et al., 2010; Park et al., 2008), Lin28 (Nathan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018a), Socs3/Jak (Smith et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2011), Atf3 (Seijffers et al., 2006; Seijffers et al., 2007), and Cbp/P300 (Hutson et al., 2019; Müller et al., 2022) have been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Atf3 has been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
source: For example, genes such as Pten (Liu et al., 2010; Park et al., 2008), Lin28 (Nathan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018a), Socs3/Jak (Smith et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2011), Atf3 (Seijffers et al., 2006; Seijffers et al., 2007), and Cbp/P300 (Hutson et al., 2019; Müller et al., 2022) have been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Cbp/P300 has been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
source: For example, genes such as Pten (Liu et al., 2010; Park et al., 2008), Lin28 (Nathan et al., 2020; Wang et al., 2018a), Socs3/Jak (Smith et al., 2009; Sun et al., 2011), Atf3 (Seijffers et al., 2006; Seijffers et al., 2007), and Cbp/P300 (Hutson et al., 2019; Müller et al., 2022) have been shown to regulate axon regeneration in different types of CNS and PNS neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Most genes and pathways that regulate axon regeneration act by altering transcriptional programs.
source: Noticeably, most of these genes and pathways act by altering transcriptional programs.
evidence: This is an observation based on the cited literature.

claim: It is unknown whether mRNA splicing and stability control are involved in axon regeneration.
source: However, transcription is the first step of gene expression. For efficient protein translation, mRNA splicing and stability control are important, but it is unknown whether these processes are involved in axon regeneration.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge.

claim: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is the most abundant internal modification of mRNA.
source: N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most abundant internal modification of mRNA, plays important roles in diverse physiological and pathological processes (Desrosiers et al., 1975; Frye and Blanco, 2016).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations.

claim: m6A plays important roles in diverse physiological and pathological processes.
source: N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most abundant internal modification of mRNA, plays important roles in diverse physiological and pathological processes (Desrosiers et al., 1975; Frye and Blanco, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: In eukaryotic cells, m6A is added by a methyltransferase complex consisting of METTL3, METTL14, WTAP, or other components.
source: In eukaryotic cells, m6A is added by a methyltransferase complex consisting of METTL3, METTL14, WTAP, or other components, is removed by demethylases FTO and ALKBH5 (Zaccara et al., 2019), and is recognized by recognition proteins, including the YTHDF family (YTHDF1, YTHDF2, and YTHDF3), YTHDC1, YTHDC2, and IGF2BP family (IGF2BP1, IGF2BP2, and IGF2BP3) (He and He, 2021; Murakami and Jaffrey, 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: m6A is removed by demethylases FTO and ALKBH5.
source: In eukaryotic cells, m6A is added by a methyltransferase complex consisting of METTL3, METTL14, WTAP, or other components, is removed by demethylases FTO and ALKBH5 (Zaccara et al., 2019), and is recognized by recognition proteins, including the YTHDF family (YTHDF1, YTHDF2, and YTHDF3), YTHDC1, YTHDC2, and IGF2BP family (IGF2BP1, IGF2BP2, and IGF2BP3) (He and He, 2021; Murakami and Jaffrey, 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: m6A is recognized by recognition proteins, including the YTHDF family (YTHDF1, YTHDF2, and YTHDF3), YTHDC1, YTHDC2, and IGF2BP family (IGF2BP1, IGF2BP2, and IGF2BP3).
source: In eukaryotic cells, m6A is added by a methyltransferase complex consisting of METTL3, METTL14, WTAP, or other components, is removed by demethylases FTO and ALKBH5 (Zaccara et al., 2019), and is recognized by recognition proteins, including the YTHDF family (YTHDF1, YTHDF2, and YTHDF3), YTHDC1, YTHDC2, and IGF2BP family (IGF2BP1, IGF2BP2, and IGF2BP3) (He and He, 2021; Murakami and Jaffrey, 2022).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: m6A exerts critical molecular functions, including RNA splicing, localization, decay, and translation.
source: Increasing evidence indicates that m6A exerts critical several molecular functions, including RNA splicing, localization, decay, and translation (Alarcón et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2015; Xiao et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The m6A level of regeneration-associated genes is altered in DRG neurons following sciatic nerve injury.
source: Interestingly, a recent study showed that the m6A level of regeneration-associated genes is altered in DRG neurons following sciatic nerve injury, and that the m6A methyltransferase complex component METTL14 or m6A-binding protein YTHDF1 supports nerve regeneration through effects on the protein translation process in the PNS (Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: The m6A methyltransferase complex component METTL14 supports nerve regeneration through effects on the protein translation process in the PNS.
source: Interestingly, a recent study showed that the m6A level of regeneration-associated genes is altered in DRG neurons following sciatic nerve injury, and that the m6A methyltransferase complex component METTL14 or m6A-binding protein YTHDF1 supports nerve regeneration through effects on the protein translation process in the PNS (Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: The m6A-binding protein YTHDF1 supports nerve regeneration through effects on the protein translation process in the PNS.
source: Interestingly, a recent study showed that the m6A level of regeneration-associated genes is altered in DRG neurons following sciatic nerve injury, and that the m6A methyltransferase complex component METTL14 or m6A-binding protein YTHDF1 supports nerve regeneration through effects on the protein translation process in the PNS (Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: The RNA levels of genes involved in RNA m6A modification were not significantly changed following sciatic nerve crush.
source: QRT-PCR analysis showed that the RNA levels of the genes involved in RNA m6A modification were not significantly changed following SNC.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the study.

claim: Mettl3, Wtap, Fto, Alkbh5, Ythdc1, and Ythdf1-3 were expressed in DRG with relatively high abundance.
source: Given that Mettl3, Wtap, Fto, Alkbh5, Ythdc1, and Ythdf1-3 were expressed in DRG with relatively high abundance (Figure 1B), we selected these genes to perform RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated functional screening through an in vitro neurite regrowth assay (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This statement is based on data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Neurite outgrowth induced by cell replating was significantly enhanced by silencing Alkbh5 or Ythdf3.
source: We found that the neurite outgrowth induced by cell replating was significantly enhanced by silencing Alkbh5 or Ythdf3 (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the study, shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: ALKBH5 knockdown exhibited the most dominant phenotype in neurite outgrowth.
source: ALKBH5 knockdown exhibited the most dominant phenotype and was chosen for subsequent research.
evidence: This is an observation from the screening experiment.

claim: ALKBH5 protein was predominantly distributed in the cytoplasm of the soma of DRG neuron.
source: The results showed that ALKBH5 protein was predominantly distributed in the cytoplasm of the soma of DRG neuron and was downregulated following SNC (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from immunofluorescent staining, shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: ALKBH5 protein was downregulated following sciatic nerve crush.
source: The results showed that ALKBH5 protein was predominantly distributed in the cytoplasm of the soma of DRG neuron and was downregulated following SNC (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from immunofluorescent staining, shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: Approximately 51.9% of NF200-positive neurons were labeled with ALKBH5.
source: Approximately 51.9% of neurofilament-200 (NF200, a marker for medium/large DRG neurons and myelinated A-fibers) positive neurons were labeled with ALKBH5, constituting 18.5% and 30.5% of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP, a marker for small peptidergic DRG neurons) and isolectin B4 (IB4, a marker for small non-peptidergic DRG neurons)-positive neurons, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from immunofluorescent staining, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: 18.5% of CGRP-positive neurons were labeled with ALKBH5.
source: Approximately 51.9% of neurofilament-200 (NF200, a marker for medium/large DRG neurons and myelinated A-fibers) positive neurons were labeled with ALKBH5, constituting 18.5% and 30.5% of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP, a marker for small peptidergic DRG neurons) and isolectin B4 (IB4, a marker for small non-peptidergic DRG neurons)-positive neurons, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from immunofluorescent staining, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: 30.5% of IB4-positive neurons were labeled with ALKBH5.
source: Approximately 51.9% of neurofilament-200 (NF200, a marker for medium/large DRG neurons and myelinated A-fibers) positive neurons were labeled with ALKBH5, constituting 18.5% and 30.5% of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP, a marker for small peptidergic DRG neurons) and isolectin B4 (IB4, a marker for small non-peptidergic DRG neurons)-positive neurons, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from immunofluorescent staining, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Western blot validated the markedly reduced expression of ALKBH5 protein in the DRGs following sciatic nerve crush.
source: Western blot further validated the markedly reduced expression of ALKBH5 protein in the DRGs following SNC (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from western blot, shown in Figure 1G and H.

claim: H205 is the conserved site of ALKBH5 for RNA demethylase activity in rats.
source: Our results indicate that the ALKBH5 protein level is dramatically reduced in DRG neurons after SNC, and that ALKBH5 inhibition enhances sciatic nerve regeneration. Furthermore, our study revealed that H205 is the conserved site of ALKBH5 for RNA demethylase activity in rats, and the mutation of H205A almost completely diminished the m6A modification activity.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the study.

claim: The mutation of H205A almost completely diminished the m6A modification activity of ALKBH5.
source: Our results indicate that the ALKBH5 protein level is dramatically reduced in DRG neurons after SNC, and that ALKBH5 inhibition enhances sciatic nerve regeneration. Furthermore, our study revealed that H205 is the conserved site of ALKBH5 for RNA demethylase activity in rats, and the mutation of H205A almost completely diminished the m6A modification activity.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the study.

claim: The axon length was significantly decreased in the wt-ALKBH5 group compared to the control group.
source: The results showed that the axon length was significantly decreased in the wt-ALKBH5 group, but not in the mut-ALKBH5 group, compared to that in the control group (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vitro neurite regrowth assay, shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The axon length was not significantly changed in the mut-ALKBH5 group compared to the control group.
source: The results showed that the axon length was significantly decreased in the wt-ALKBH5 group, but not in the mut-ALKBH5 group, compared to that in the control group (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vitro neurite regrowth assay, shown in Figure 2E.

claim: ALKBH5 overexpression in sensory neurons reduced axonal regeneration past the crush site.
source: The result indicated that ALKBH5 overexpression in sensory neurons reduced axonal regeneration past the crush site, while mutant ALKBH5 had no significant effect (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vivo sciatic nerve regeneration assay, shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Mutant ALKBH5 had no significant effect on axonal regeneration past the crush site.
source: The result indicated that ALKBH5 overexpression in sensory neurons reduced axonal regeneration past the crush site, while mutant ALKBH5 had no significant effect (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vivo sciatic nerve regeneration assay, shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The maximum axon length was dramatically attenuated in the wt-ALKBH5 group but was not significantly changed in the mut-ALKBH5 group compared to the control group.
source: The maximum axon length was also dramatically attenuated in the wt-ALKBH5 group but was not significantly changed in the mut-ALKBH5 group compared to that in the control group (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vivo sciatic nerve regeneration assay, shown in Figure 2I.

claim: ALKBH5 inhibits axonal regeneration in an m6A-dependent manner.
source: These data indicate that ALKBH5 inhibits axonal regeneration in an m6A-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing that wild-type but not mutant ALKBH5 affects axon regeneration.

claim: ALKBH5 deficiency either in the Alkbh5-shRNA1 (KD1) or Alkbh5-shRNA2 (KD2) group significantly increased the axon length compared to the control shRNA (NC) group.
source: The results showed that ALKBH5 deficiency either in the Alkbh5-shRNA1 (KD1) or Alkbh5-shRNA2 (KD2) group significantly increased the axon length compared to that in the control shRNA (NC) group (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vitro neurite regrowth assay, shown in Figure 3C–E.

claim: ALKBH5 knockdown significantly enhanced axon outgrowth in the presence of inhibitory substrates CSPGs.
source: The data showed that ALKBH5 knockdown significantly enhanced axon outgrowth in the presence of inhibitory substrates (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vitro neurite regrowth assay with CSPGs, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The extension of SCG10-positive axons and the maximum axon length of the sciatic nerve were significantly increased following ALKBH5 knockdown compared to the control group after sciatic nerve crush.
source: The results showed that the extension of SCG10-positive axons and the maximum axon length of the sciatic nerve were significantly increased following ALKBH5 knockdown compared to the control group after SNC (Figure 3G–I).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vivo sciatic nerve regeneration assay, shown in Figure 3G–I.

claim: 0.5 μM Z56957173 presented a significant promotion effect on axon growth.
source: Next, we chose two dose of the two SAI respectively to perform the in vitro neurite regrowth assay and observed that 0.5 μM Z56957173 presented a significant promotion effect on axon growth.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vitro neurite regrowth assay with selective ALKBH5 inhibitors.

claim: Significantly increased axon length was observed in the neurons treated with 10 μM Z52453295.
source: Meanwhile, the significantly increased axon length was also observed in the neurons treated with 10 μM Z52453295 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and D).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vitro neurite regrowth assay with selective ALKBH5 inhibitors, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C and D.

claim: Z52453295 significantly increased the length of the maximum regenerated axon at 6.25 and 25 mM after sciatic nerve crush.
source: The results showed that Z52453295 significantly increased the length of the maximum regenerated axon at 6.25 and 25 mM after SNC (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and F).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vivo sciatic nerve regeneration assay with selective ALKBH5 inhibitors, shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E and F.

claim: ALKBH5 inhibition by selective ALKBH5 inhibitors promoted axon regeneration after nerve injury.
source: These results indicated that ALKBH5 inhibition by SAI promoted axon regeneration after nerve injury and suggested the therapeutic potential of modulating ALKBH5 function with SAI in nerve injury repair.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings with selective ALKBH5 inhibitors.

claim: Quite a few genes were enriched in the metabolism pathway after ALKBH5 inhibition.
source: Interestingly, the results showed that quite a few genes were enriched in the metabolism pathway after ALKBH5 inhibition (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from KEGG enrichment analysis of RNA-Seq data, shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Several metabolism-related genes, including Aldh3b1, Galns, Ndufa11, Lpin2, Pold1, Cox8a, and St6gal1, were significantly downregulated following ALKBH5 knockdown.
source: The expression of these genes was validated using qRT-PCR, which showed that several metabolism-related genes, including Aldh3b1, Galns, Ndufa11, Lpin2, Pold1, Cox8a, and St6gal1, were significantly downregulated following ALKBH5 knockdown (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from qRT-PCR validation, shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The m6A enrichment of Aldh3b1, Lpin2, and Galns was increased on day 3 following sciatic nerve crush.
source: Next, we examined the potential m6A modification in these genes (p<0.01) by MeRIP-qPCR analysis and found that the m6A enrichment of Aldh3b1, Lpin2, and Galns was increased on day 3 following SNC (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from MeRIP-qPCR analysis, shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Interfering the expression of Lpin2 significantly increased the neurite length of primary DRG neurons.
source: RNAi-mediated functional screening was performed to explore the role of these genes in neurite regrowth, which showed that interfering the expression of Lpin2 significantly increased the neurite length of primary DRG neurons (Figure 4D and E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that Lpin2 is a target of ALKBH5 during the axonal regeneration of DRG neurons.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from RNAi-mediated functional screening, shown in Figure 4D and E.

claim: Lpin2 is a target of ALKBH5 during the axonal regeneration of DRG neurons.
source: RNAi-mediated functional screening was performed to explore the role of these genes in neurite regrowth, which showed that interfering the expression of Lpin2 significantly increased the neurite length of primary DRG neurons (Figure 4D and E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that Lpin2 is a target of ALKBH5 during the axonal regeneration of DRG neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNAi-mediated functional screening results.

claim: The m6A level in Lpin2 mature mRNA, but not in pre-mRNA, was significantly increased on day 3 post sciatic nerve crush compared to that in intact animals.
source: MeRIP-qPCR analysis showed that the m6A level in Lpin2 mature mRNA, but not in pre-mRNA, was significantly increased on day 3 post SNC compared to that in intact animals (Figure 4C, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A), which showed an opposite trend compared to that of ALKBH5 (Figure 1E–H).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from MeRIP-qPCR analysis, shown in Figure 4C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: ALKBH5 downregulation contributes to the increase in m6A in Lpin2 mature mRNA.
source: These results suggest that ALKBH5 downregulation contributes to the increase in m6A in Lpin2 mature mRNA.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that ALKBH5 and m6A levels in Lpin2 show opposite trends after SNC.

claim: ALKBH5 knockdown increased the m6A enrichment of Lpin2 mature mRNA.
source: Furthermore, MeRIP-qPCR assay showed that ALKBH5 knockdown increased the m6A enrichment of Lpin2 mature mRNA, whereas wt-ALKBH5, but not mut-ALKBH5, decreased the m6A level of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from MeRIP-qPCR assay, shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: wt-ALKBH5, but not mut-ALKBH5, decreased the m6A level of Lpin2 mature mRNA.
source: Furthermore, MeRIP-qPCR assay showed that ALKBH5 knockdown increased the m6A enrichment of Lpin2 mature mRNA, whereas wt-ALKBH5, but not mut-ALKBH5, decreased the m6A level of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from MeRIP-qPCR assay, shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: ALKBH5 knockdown reduced the expression of Lpin2 mature mRNA.
source: ALKBH5 knockdown reduced the expression of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5C), but not the Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), whereas overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the level of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5D), but not that of Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from qRT-PCR analysis, shown in Figure 5C.

claim: ALKBH5 knockdown did not affect the expression of Lpin2 pre-mRNA.
source: ALKBH5 knockdown reduced the expression of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5C), but not the Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), whereas overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the level of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5D), but not that of Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from qRT-PCR analysis, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the level of Lpin2 mature mRNA.
source: ALKBH5 knockdown reduced the expression of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5C), but not the Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), whereas overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the level of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5D), but not that of Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from qRT-PCR analysis, shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Overexpression of wt-ALKBH5 or mut-ALKBH5 did not affect the level of Lpin2 pre-mRNA.
source: ALKBH5 knockdown reduced the expression of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5C), but not the Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), whereas overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the level of Lpin2 mature mRNA (Figure 5D), but not that of Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from qRT-PCR analysis, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: ALKBH5 knockdown downregulated the LPIN2 protein level.
source: The western blot assay showed that ALKBH5 knockdown downregulated the LPIN2 protein level (Figure 5E and F), whereas overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the LPIN2 protein expression (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from western blot assay, shown in Figure 5E and F.

claim: Overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the LPIN2 protein expression.
source: The western blot assay showed that ALKBH5 knockdown downregulated the LPIN2 protein level (Figure 5E and F), whereas overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the LPIN2 protein expression (Figure 5G and H).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from western blot assay, shown in Figure 5G and H.

claim: Lpin2 mRNA is a target of ALKBH5-mediated demethylation.
source: These data suggest that Lpin2 mRNA is a target of ALKBH5-mediated demethylation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing that ALKBH5 affects m6A levels, mRNA stability, and protein expression of Lpin2.

claim: The half-life of Lpin2 mature mRNA in ALKBH5-knockdown DRG neurons was significantly shorter than that in control cells.
source: We found that the half-life of Lpin2 mature mRNA in ALKBH5-knockdown DRG neurons was significantly shorter than that in control cells (Figure 5I), although there was no significant difference in the level of remaining Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from RNA stability assay, shown in Figure 5I.

claim: There was no significant difference in the level of remaining Lpin2 pre-mRNA between ALKBH5-knockdown and control DRG neurons.
source: We found that the half-life of Lpin2 mature mRNA in ALKBH5-knockdown DRG neurons was significantly shorter than that in control cells (Figure 5I), although there was no significant difference in the level of remaining Lpin2 pre-mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from RNA stability assay, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The half-life of Lpin2 mature mRNA was upregulated in neurons with overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, compared to that in the neurons with EGFP overexpression.
source: Furthermore, the half-life of Lpin2 mature mRNA was upregulated in neurons with overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, compared to that in the neurons with EGFP overexpression (Figure 5J).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from RNA stability assay, shown in Figure 5J.

claim: There were no significant changes in the Lpin2 pre mRNA half-life with ALKBH5 overexpression.
source: In contrast, there were no significant changes in the Lpin2 pre mRNA (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from RNA stability assay, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E.

claim: ALKBH5 regulates mRNA stability through m6A sites located in the 3' UTR region near the stop codon.
source: Previous studies have shown that ALKBH5 regulates mRNA stability through m6A sites located in the 3' UTR region near the stop codon (Tang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The GGACA motif with the highest prediction score in the 3' UTR region near the stop codon is the candidate site involved in Lpin2 mRNA stability regulation.
source: In the present work, by using SRAMP (Zhou et al., 2016), we predicted the specific m6A modification sites of Lpin2 and identified the GGACA motif with the highest prediction score in the 3' UTR region near the stop codon as the candidate site involved in Lpin2 mRNA stability regulation (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a finding from computational prediction using SRAMP, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: The m6A level at motif GGACA in Lpin2 3' UTR region was significantly increased in ALKBH5 knockdown DRG neurons compared with NC.
source: With the probe targeting GGACA, we found that the m6A level at motif GGACA in Lpin2 3' UTR region was significantly increased in ALKBH5 knockdown DRG neurons compared with NC.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from SELECT-m6A analysis.

claim: Overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not mut-ALKBH5, reduced the m6A level at motif GGACA in Lpin2 3' UTR region.
source: Moreover, overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not mut-ALKBH5, reduced the m6A level at motif GGACA (Figure 5K and L).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from SELECT-m6A analysis, shown in Figure 5K and L.

claim: ALKBH5 knockdown decreased the activity of the luciferase vector containing the 3′UTR of Lpin2 mRNA.
source: The results showed that ALKBH5 knockdown decreased the activity of the luciferase vector containing the 3′UTR of Lpin2 mRNA, while overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the luciferase activity.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from luciferase reporter assay.

claim: Overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the luciferase activity of the vector containing the 3′UTR of Lpin2 mRNA.
source: The results showed that ALKBH5 knockdown decreased the activity of the luciferase vector containing the 3′UTR of Lpin2 mRNA, while overexpression of wt-ALKBH5, but not of mut-ALKBH5, increased the luciferase activity.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from luciferase reporter assay.

claim: Mutation of the luciferase reporter at the potential m6A site (A to C) almost completely reinstated the luciferase activity when ALKBH5 was knocked down or overexpressed.
source: Mutation of the luciferase reporter at the potential m6A site (A to C) almost completely reinstated the luciferase activity when ALKBH5 was knocked down or overexpressed (Figure 5M and N).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from luciferase reporter assay, shown in Figure 5M and N.

claim: ALKBH5 upregulates the level of Lpin2 mature mRNA by increasing its stability through m6A in the 3' UTR.
source: These data indicate that ALKBH5 upregulates the level of Lpin2 mature mRNA by increasing its stability through m6A in the 3' UTR.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings on m6A levels, mRNA stability, and luciferase reporter assays.

claim: LPIN2 is a phosphatidic acid phosphatase enzyme that plays a central role in the penultimate step of the glycerol phosphate pathway.
source: LPIN2, a phosphatidic acid phosphatase enzyme, plays a central role in the penultimate step of the glycerol phosphate pathway and catalyzes the conversion of phosphatidic acid (PA) to diacylglycerol (DG) in coordination with LPIN1 (Donkor et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: LPIN2 catalyzes the conversion of phosphatidic acid (PA) to diacylglycerol (DG) in coordination with LPIN1.
source: LPIN2, a phosphatidic acid phosphatase enzyme, plays a central role in the penultimate step of the glycerol phosphate pathway and catalyzes the conversion of phosphatidic acid (PA) to diacylglycerol (DG) in coordination with LPIN1 (Donkor et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: LPIN1 has a pivotal function in retina axonal regeneration.
source: Recent reports have indicated the pivotal function of LPIN1 in retina axonal regeneration (Yang et al., 2020); however, the role of LPIN2 in sciatic nerve regeneration remains unknown.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a recent report.

claim: The expression of Lpin2 mRNA decreased following sciatic nerve crush.
source: We found decreased expression of Lpin2 mRNA (Figure 6A) and protein following SNC (Figure 6B and C), indicating that Lpin2 is an injury-reduced gene.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from qRT-PCR, shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The expression of LPIN2 protein decreased following sciatic nerve crush.
source: We found decreased expression of Lpin2 mRNA (Figure 6A) and protein following SNC (Figure 6B and C), indicating that Lpin2 is an injury-reduced gene.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from western blot, shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Lpin2 is an injury-reduced gene.
source: We found decreased expression of Lpin2 mRNA (Figure 6A) and protein following SNC (Figure 6B and C), indicating that Lpin2 is an injury-reduced gene.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that Lpin2 expression decreases after SNC.

claim: The axon length in DRG neurons with LPIN2 overexpressed was significantly decreased compared to that in the control group.
source: To further explore the direct role of LPIN2 in axonal regeneration, we first examined the function of LPIN2 in neurite outgrowth in vitro and observed that the axon length in DRG neurons with LPIN2 overexpressed was significantly decreased compared to that in the control group (Figure 6D–F).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vitro neurite outgrowth assay, shown in Figure 6D–F.

claim: LPIN2 overexpression reduced the axonal regeneration index.
source: The results showed that LPIN2 overexpression reduced the axonal regeneration index (Figure 6G and H) and maximum length of the regenerated sciatic nerve (Figure 6I), suggesting that LPIN2 impairs sciatic nerve regeneration following SNC.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vivo sciatic nerve regeneration assay, shown in Figure 6G and H.

claim: LPIN2 overexpression reduced the maximum length of the regenerated sciatic nerve.
source: The results showed that LPIN2 overexpression reduced the axonal regeneration index (Figure 6G and H) and maximum length of the regenerated sciatic nerve (Figure 6I), suggesting that LPIN2 impairs sciatic nerve regeneration following SNC.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vivo sciatic nerve regeneration assay, shown in Figure 6I.

claim: LPIN2 impairs sciatic nerve regeneration following sciatic nerve crush.
source: The results showed that LPIN2 overexpression reduced the axonal regeneration index (Figure 6G and H) and maximum length of the regenerated sciatic nerve (Figure 6I), suggesting that LPIN2 impairs sciatic nerve regeneration following SNC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings showing that LPIN2 overexpression reduces axon regeneration.

claim: DRG neurons with overexpressed LPIN2 had an increased presence of visible lipid droplets containing triglycerides.
source: To further investigate the link between lipid droplets and LPIN2 in axon regeneration, we examined DRG neurons with overexpressed LPIN2 and found that these neurons had an increased presence of visible lipid droplets containing triglycerides, unlike the control group (Figure 6J and K).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from lipid droplet staining, shown in Figure 6J and K.

claim: LPIN2 plays an important role in regulating axon regeneration by modulating lipid metabolism.
source: Therefore, our findings suggest that LPIN2 plays an important role in regulating axon regeneration by modulating lipid metabolism.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings on LPIN2 overexpression and lipid droplet accumulation.

claim: LPIN2 could diminish the promoting effect of ALKBH5 deficiency on neurite outgrowth.
source: The results showed that LPIN2 could diminish the promoting effect of ALKBH5 deficiency on neurite outgrowth (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vitro neurite regrowth assay, shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: LPIN2 largely restored the increased regeneration index and length of the maximum regenerated axon in vivo in ALKBH5-deficient animals following sciatic nerve crush.
source: Furthermore, LPIN2 largely restored the increased regeneration index and length of the maximum regenerated axon in vivo in ALKBH5-deficient animals following SNC (Figure 7C–E).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the in vivo sciatic nerve regeneration assay, shown in Figure 7C–E.

claim: ALKBH5-deficiency induces axonal regeneration through LPIN2 following sciatic nerve crush.
source: Taken together, ALKBH5-deficiency induces axonal regeneration through LPIN2 following SNC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the rescue experiments showing that LPIN2 overexpression reverses the effects of ALKBH5 knockdown.

claim: No significant change in ALKBH5 expression was observed after optic nerve crush.
source: In contrast to the expression in the DRG, no significant change in ALKBH5 expression was observed after ONC (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from immunofluorescent staining, shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: Approximately 70.85 ± 8.85% RGCs were successfully infected with AAV2/2 expressing EGFP.
source: Two weeks later, we observed successful infection of approximately 70.85 ± 8.85% RGCs (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from immunofluorescent staining, shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: ALKBH5 knockdown increased the RGC survival rates compared to the control group following optic nerve crush.
source: By quantifying the numbers of Tuj1-positive cells in the retina, we found that ALKBH5 knockdown increased the RGC survival rates compared to the control group following ONC (Figure 8D and E).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from quantification of Tuj1-positive cells, shown in Figure 8D and E.

claim: The number of regenerated axons was increased in the ALKBH5 knockdown group compared to the control group.
source: Moreover, the number of regenerated axons was increased in the ALKBH5 knockdown group compared to the control group, and the maximum length of axons crossing the lesion site in ALKBH5 knockdown mice was up to 1.2 mm at 2 wk after ONC (Figure 8F and G).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from CTB labeling, shown in Figure 8F and G.

claim: The maximum length of axons crossing the lesion site in ALKBH5 knockdown mice was up to 1.2 mm at 2 wk after optic nerve crush.
source: Moreover, the number of regenerated axons was increased in the ALKBH5 knockdown group compared to the control group, and the maximum length of axons crossing the lesion site in ALKBH5 knockdown mice was up to 1.2 mm at 2 wk after ONC (Figure 8F and G).
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from CTB labeling, shown in Figure 8F and G.

claim: Inhibition of ALKBH5 promotes the survival and axonal regeneration of RGCs in the CNS.
source: These data indicate that inhibition of ALKBH5 promotes the survival and axonal regeneration of RGCs in the CNS.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings on RGC survival and axon regeneration after ALKBH5 knockdown.

claim: During axonal regeneration, injured neurons must first survive and convert to the regenerative gene expression mode.
source: During axonal regeneration, injured neurons must first survive and convert to the regenerative gene expression mode (Chandran et al., 2016; Scheib and Höke, 2013; Sun et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: ALKBH5 plays a critical role in axonal regeneration after nerve injury.
source: The present study showed that ALKBH5 plays a critical role in axonal regeneration after nerve injury.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's main finding.

claim: The ALKBH5 protein level was reduced in DRG neurons following sciatic nerve crush, which enhanced neurite outgrowth in vitro and sciatic nerve regeneration in vivo.
source: The ALKBH5 protein level was reduced in DRG neurons following SNC, which enhanced neurite outgrowth in vitro and sciatic nerve regeneration in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's findings.

claim: The induced axonal regeneration following ALKBH5 knockdown is driven by downregulated Lpin2 with increased m6A modification on its 3′ UTR.
source: Mechanistically, the induced axonal regeneration following ALKBH5 knockdown is driven by downregulated Lpin2 with increased m6A modification on its 3′ UTR.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's mechanistic findings.

claim: RNA m6A modification plays a critical role in neural development.
source: Several reports have indicated that RNA m6A modification plays a critical role in neural development (Haussmann et al., 2016; Lence et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2018b; Yoon et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: m6A methylation is important for transcriptional pre-patterning in mammalian cortical neurogenesis.
source: For example, m6A methylation is important for transcriptional pre-patterning in mammalian cortical neurogenesis and embryonic neural stem cell self-renewal (Wang et al., 2018b; Yoon et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: m6A methylation is important for embryonic neural stem cell self-renewal.
source: For example, m6A methylation is important for transcriptional pre-patterning in mammalian cortical neurogenesis and embryonic neural stem cell self-renewal (Wang et al., 2018b; Yoon et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: The m6A level is dynamically changed during neurite extension in neuronal development.
source: Additionally, the m6A level is dynamically changed during neurite extension in neuronal development (Lence et al., 2016; Yoon et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: The increased expression of RNA m6A demethylase FTO contributes to spinal nerve ligation-induced neuropathic pain in mice.
source: The function of m6A modification in DRGs has recently gained attention, with one study demonstrating that the increased expression of RNA m6A demethylase FTO contributes to spinal nerve ligation-induced neuropathic pain in mice (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Conditional knockout of the m6A writer Mettl14 in mice impairs sciatic nerve regeneration.
source: Another study revealed that conditional knockout of the m6A writer Mettl14, or reader Ythdf1 in mice impairs sciatic nerve regeneration (Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Conditional knockout of the m6A reader Ythdf1 in mice impairs sciatic nerve regeneration.
source: Another study revealed that conditional knockout of the m6A writer Mettl14, or reader Ythdf1 in mice impairs sciatic nerve regeneration (Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: m6A modification plays significant roles in physiological and pathological processes of DRG neurons.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that m6A modification plays significant roles in physiological and pathological processes of DRG neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cited literature.

claim: Deletion of m6A writer METTL14 inhibited axon regeneration.
source: In principle, the function of m6A modification requires the joint participation of m6A writer, reader, and eraser. Weng et al. have reported that deletion of m6A writer METTL14 or reader YTHDF1 inhibited axon regeneration (Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Deletion of m6A reader YTHDF1 inhibited axon regeneration.
source: In principle, the function of m6A modification requires the joint participation of m6A writer, reader, and eraser. Weng et al. have reported that deletion of m6A writer METTL14 or reader YTHDF1 inhibited axon regeneration (Weng et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: YTHDF3 is a novel regulator of axonal regeneration.
source: Instead, we identified another reader YTHDF3 as a novel regulator of axonal regeneration.
evidence: This is a finding from the functional screening in the study.

claim: ALKBH5 is an RNA demethylase, widely expressed in adult neurons and decreased during brain development.
source: ALKBH5 is an RNA demethylase, widely expressed in adult neurons and decreased during brain development (Du et al., 2020), that regulates mRNA metabolism and translation via m6A demethylation of the transcript (Xu et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: ALKBH5 regulates mRNA metabolism and translation via m6A demethylation of the transcript.
source: ALKBH5 is an RNA demethylase, widely expressed in adult neurons and decreased during brain development (Du et al., 2020), that regulates mRNA metabolism and translation via m6A demethylation of the transcript (Xu et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: The H204A mutation in human ALKBH5 resulted in a complete loss of m6A modification activity.
source: Similar result were observed for ALKBH5-induced osteoblast differentiation (Feng et al., 2021), in which the H204A mutation in human ALKBH5 resulted in a complete loss of m6A modification activity (Feng et al., 2014; Zheng et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: LPIN2 is a key player in the canonical pathway that regulates lipid metabolism.
source: We also demonstrated that ALKBH5 regulates axonal regeneration in the PNS by modulating, at least in part, LPIN2. LPIN2 is a key player in the canonical pathway that regulates lipid metabolism (Eaton et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: ALKBH5 modulates the Lpin2 mature mRNA stability through its m6A demethylase activity.
source: We provide convincing evidence that ALKBH5 modulates the Lpin2 mature mRNA stability through its m6A demethylase activity.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the study's mechanistic findings.

claim: ALKBH5 downregulates the mature Lpin2 mRNA through its RNA m6A demethylase activity.
source: Thus, we believe that ALKBH5 downregulates the mature Lpin2 mRNA through its RNA m6A demethylase activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Injured neurons need a large supply of lipids for cell membrane formation during axonal regeneration.
source: Injured neurons need a large supply of lipids for cell membrane formation during axonal regeneration (Bradke et al., 2012; Pfenninger, 2009; Vance et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Lipid metabolism plays a critical role in axonal regeneration.
source: Yang et al. have demonstrated that lipid metabolism plays a critical role in axonal regeneration (Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The induced axonal regeneration ability of the ALKBH5-inhibited animals may be attributed to the appropriate lipid metabolism in DRG neurons.
source: As LPIN2 is a master regulator of lipid metabolism, the induced axonal regeneration ability of the ALKBH5-inhibited animals in this study may be attributed to the appropriate lipid metabolism in DRG neurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings and the known role of LPIN2 in lipid metabolism.

claim: Forced expression of LPIN2 largely impaired the axonal regeneration induced by ALKBH5 deficiency.
source: The retention of the lipid droplets was observed in LPIN2 overexpressed neurons, and the rescue experiment indicated that forced expression of LPIN2 largely impaired the axonal regeneration induced by ALKBH5 deficiency.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from the rescue experiment.

claim: This is the first study to demonstrate that rewiring neuronal lipid metabolism during axonal regeneration is regulated by RNA m6A modification.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to demonstrate that rewiring neuronal lipid metabolism during axonal regeneration is regulated by RNA m6A modification, which may serve as a therapeutic target for nerve injury repair.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study's findings.

claim: ALKBH5 expression was unchanged in the RGCs following optic nerve crush.
source: In contrast to the observations in DRG neurons, ALKBH5 expression was unchanged in the RGCs following ONC, which may partially contribute to the different regenerative abilities between neurons in the PNS and CNS.
evidence: This is a direct experimental finding from immunofluorescent staining.

claim: The unchanged ALKBH5 expression in RGCs may partially contribute to the different regenerative abilities between neurons in the PNS and CNS.
source: In contrast to the observations in DRG neurons, ALKBH5 expression was unchanged in the RGCs following ONC, which may partially contribute to the different regenerative abilities between neurons in the PNS and CNS.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observation of differential ALKBH5 expression in PNS and CNS.

claim: The methyltransferase METTL14 is essential for retinal photoreceptor survival.
source: Previous studies have reported that the methyltransferase METTL14 is essential for retinal photoreceptor survival, while inhibition of m6A demethylases FTO supports the survival of dopamine neurons (Selberg et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2022), suggesting that m6A plays important roles in neuronal survival.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: Inhibition of m6A demethylases FTO supports the survival of dopamine neurons.
source: Previous studies have reported that the methyltransferase METTL14 is essential for retinal photoreceptor survival, while inhibition of m6A demethylases FTO supports the survival of dopamine neurons (Selberg et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2022), suggesting that m6A plays important roles in neuronal survival.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: m6A plays important roles in neuronal survival.
source: Previous studies have reported that the methyltransferase METTL14 is essential for retinal photoreceptor survival, while inhibition of m6A demethylases FTO supports the survival of dopamine neurons (Selberg et al., 2021; Yang et al., 2022), suggesting that m6A plays important roles in neuronal survival.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cited literature.

claim: This is the first study to report that manipulating m6A-related proteins could induce axonal regeneration in the CNS.
source: In addition, to the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to report that manipulating m6A-related proteins could induce axonal regeneration in the CNS.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study's findings.

claim: Blocking ALKBH5 has potential clinical application in neuronal injury repair both in the PNS and CNS.
source: Our study suggests that blocking ALKBH5 has potential clinical application in neuronal injury repair both in the PNS and CNS.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.
